description: §6.4 affine non-composability and the delta counterparts that are composable. Conversion arithmetic lives in the factors category.

cases.rationale: A bare affine unit is valid; only compound expressions are forbidden.
Unambiguously compound. Degree-Celsius-hours is not a meaningful quantity: the offset makes the product depend on the arbitrary zero of the scale.
One term with a redundant exponent of 1 is the same expression as a bare symbol, so it is not compound. "Compound" is never defined in §6.4; this case pins the boundary.
A single term, but squaring an affine scale is as meaningless as multiplying two of them. The rule is one term with exponent 1, not one term.

The ordering of the affine check against §6.3 step 2 is observable here. Check before merging and this fails; check after merging and it is dimensionless and passes. AMB-017 recommends checking the parsed term list, so this fails — and the error names what the user actually wrote.

Same check-ordering question as parsing.affine.005, but merging here would leave a bare degC rather than dimensionless — so a merge-first implementation returns success with canonical form degC. Rejecting is the conservative reading.
The delta counterpart shares its partner's dimension. §6.4 names delta units but never specifies them as registry entries, so their dimension and factor are assumed rather than stated.
Delta units are purely multiplicative and freely composable — a warming rate is exactly what the delta unit exists to express. This is the case that makes the affine/delta split worth the complexity.
degF is the unit that discriminates between the two readings of §6.4's conversion formula (AMB-016) — but parsing is unaffected, so this case is normative.
One composable operand does not rescue the expression. The rule is about the presence of an affine symbol anywhere, not about the other terms.
